t: Chibchan-speaking chiefdoms in Colombia's eastern highlands, led by the zipa of Bacatá in the south and the zaque of Hunza in the north.
They traded salt, cotton cloth and emeralds for gold, which their smiths cast into ornaments and votive figures offered in sacred lakes.
A small Spanish force under Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada conquered them in 1537–1540 and founded Bogotá in the zipas' lands.
dyk: A small gold raft found in a cave at Pasca in 1969 shows a Muisca chief and his attendants afloat, the kind of lake ceremony behind the legend of El Dorado.
ev: The Early Muisca period begins in the highland basins of the Eastern Ranges
Chroniclers say the zipa Saguamanchica and zaque Michuá both die in battle near Chocontá
Tisquesusa becomes zipa after Nemequene dies of a war wound
Quesada's expedition enters Muisca lands and seizes the zaque at Hunza
Santa Fe de Bogotá is founded on 6 August in the zipas' former lands
The zipa Sagipa dies after torture; Tunja is founded on 6 August
The last zaque, Aquiminzaque, is beheaded at Tunja
A gold votive raft is found in a cave at Pasca

f.capital: None single: the zipa ruled from Bacatá (near Funza), the zaque from Hunza (Tunja)
